title: The water-trial planning board
subtitle: Summer 1 • Build a method another team could follow
objective: Plan a controlled comparison of water amount and plant growth, with repeated plants and consistent records.

sow.exactOutcome: Plan an investigation into what plants need (links ASDAN allotment).
sow.alignment: Chronological continuation of the supplied SOW. This lesson develops or reviews the named outcome; it does not claim an accreditation award.

priorLearning: Height and leaf condition provide different clues.
success: Plan repeated plants, dates and a height rule.

vocabulary.meaning: Use further observations or plants to check variation.

equipment: Printed shared evidence and one chosen pupil route; pencil; optional ruler; projector or offline HTML.
Optional six matched, established young bean seedlings in labelled 200 mL pots with drainage; trays; ruler; measuring syringe or cylinder; adult-approved compost.
preparation: Print the shared evidence, one response route and exit page. Routes are alternatives, not a workload ladder.
Read the worked answers. Prepare an oral, pointing or adult-scribed route where useful.

The supplied fictional plan compares 5 and 15 mL daily for 10 days. These are teaching values, not universal watering recommendations. For a real investigation, an adult pilots suitable amounts for the species, pots and room, records any changes and checks plant welfare daily.

Optional setup can begin today: label plants A1–A3 and B1–B3, record baselines, allocate comparable seedlings across groups, and agree who maintains the record. Future observation time must be scheduled separately.
safety: Use non-toxic plants; no tasting or direct handling of fertiliser. Wash hands after handling plants or compost.
Keep water in trays away from electrical devices; wipe spills. Use needle-free measuring equipment.
An adult checks plants daily. Stop or adjust a real treatment if severe stress develops; record the change honestly. Do not overheat or seal plants in a cupboard.
practicalAlternative: All core reasoning uses the supplied evidence and can be completed in 40 minutes without a live practical.

misconceptions.claim: Changing water and light tests water alone.
misconceptions.correction: Two changes prevent separating their effects.
misconceptions.check: Ask what else could explain a difference.

misconceptions.claim: A prediction belongs in the results column.
misconceptions.correction: Predictions are expectations; results are actual measurements.
misconceptions.check: Ask whether the measurement has happened.

misconceptions.correction: Individuals vary; matched repeats improve a comparison.
misconceptions.check: Ask why each group has three seedlings.

access.supported: Short choices, word bank and pointing or adult-scribed reasons; same core scientific goal.
access.standard: Make a short evidence-based explanation or record using the supplied information.
access.stretch: Apply the core idea to a changed case, evaluate evidence or identify a limit.
access.regulation: Preview the sequence. Offer seated observation, quiet paired rehearsal, private feedback and a pass from public sharing. Routes respond to current access needs, not a diagnosis.

slides.title: A good plan can be followed by someone else
slides.notes: Explain the difference between planning now and waiting for growth later. All pupils can meet today’s planning objective on paper.

slides.title: Retrieve what makes a useful comparison
body: 2. Is height the only useful observation?
3. What unit can we use for height?
slides.notes: 1 valid requirement. 2 no; leaf colour/condition also useful. 3 centimetres.

slides.title: I repair two changes
body: The flawed plan changes water and light.
slides.notes: Think aloud: “If the groups differ, I would not know whether water or darkness mattered. I repair the light conditions before I start.” Other factors still need matching; use three comparable seedlings in each group.

visual.title: A plan with two changes
visual.description: Two groups each have three matched young seedlings. Group A receives 5 mL in light; group B receives 15 mL in darkness. Water and light both vary, so their effects cannot be separated.

elements.text: Water AND light change: the cause becomes unclear.

slides.title: I define the measurement before taking it
body: Measure to the main shoot tip.
slides.notes: Shares I do time. Think aloud: “Including the pot would add something I am not studying. I choose one start and endpoint and use them every time.” Worked reading is 6 cm.

visual.title: Use one height rule
visual.description: A ruler begins at the soil surface beside a seedling. The main shoot tip reaches 6 cm; measure from soil surface to shoot tip, without including pot height or forcing the plant straight.

elements.text: Measure the same part, from the same starting level.
Do not include the pot or straighten the shoot by force.

slides.title: I make dates and responsibilities visible
slides.notes: Shares I do time. Think aloud: “A results heading is not a result. I leave future values blank and plan who will measure.” Keep the same time of day; rotate positions within a comparable light area where useful and record method.

visual.title: Plan observations before results exist
visual.description: A timeline lays out the proposed record: baseline day 0 then days 3, 7 and 10. Each uses the same plant IDs, height rule and leaf-condition notes. Future results remain unknown.

elements.text: The plan contains actions, not made-up results.
Same observation time; record every plant, including difficulties.

slides.title: The plan-repair meeting
body: Name two things to keep comparable.
slides.notes: W1: daily water amount; height change and leaf condition; two relevant controls. Have one pupil challenge the plan and another point to a fix in the shared cards.

table.caption: Fictional teaching plan; future results are unknown

slides.title: Prediction or result?
slides.notes: W2: expectation is a prediction; the measured statement is only a result if actually measured. The class has not produced those data today. Choose a useful blank record heading and a baseline task.
slides.reveal: Predict in a separate space. Record results only after observation.

slides.title: Which plan best tests water amount?
slides.notes: Correct first option; all options need a reason.

options.text: Change water amount; keep species and growing conditions comparable.
options.feedback: This isolates the planned water comparison more effectively.

options.text: Change water amount, species and light together.
options.feedback: Several factors could explain the difference.

options.text: Write the expected heights into the results table now.

slides.title: Choose your science route
body: Audit and repair a weak plan.
slides.notes: Set ONE route. Planning is today’s assessed product. An optional class setup must use adult-piloted care levels; paper plans remain fully valid. Do not let a pupil fill unknown results to make the plan look finished.

slides.title: Make your own evidence record
slides.notes: Planning is today’s assessed product. An optional class setup must use adult-piloted care levels; paper plans remain fully valid. Do not let a pupil fill unknown results to make the plan look finished.

slides.title: Check what the evidence can show
body: Point to the clue you used.
slides.notes: Shares independent time. Ask for a reason, not just a correct word. Planning is today’s assessed product. An optional class setup must use adult-piloted care levels; paper plans remain fully valid. Do not let a pupil fill unknown results to make the plan look finished.

slides.title: Lundy loop: improve the shared account
slides.notes: Listen to a selected pupil revision and visibly adopt a scientifically accurate contribution. Offer private, written or partner feedback.
slides.prompt: Which repair would make the eventual evidence more useful?
slides.reveal: Keep one planned change, matched groups, repeated plants and a consistent dated record.

slides.title: Keep the useful change
slides.notes: Shares review time. Name how a pupil contribution changed a label, method or conclusion. Do not rank pupils.
slides.reveal: Keep one planned change, matched groups, repeated plants and a consistent dated record.

slides.title: Three final checks
body: E1. What factor is this plan changing?
E2. Why use three plants per group?
E3. Should a prediction be copied into the results as a measurement?
slides.notes: Collect brief individual evidence. Use the answer key and re-teach the specified misconception if needed.

pupilPages.title: Shared evidence • Proposed water comparison
pupilPages.intro: Fictional teaching plan. An adult must adapt any real watering method to the plants and setting.

cards.title: Question
cards.text: How does daily water amount affect growth of these young bean seedlings over 10 days?

cards.title: Groups
cards.text: A1–A3: 5 mL each daily. B1–B3: 15 mL each daily. These amounts are a fictional teaching plan.

cards.title: Keep comparable
cards.text: Species, age, starting size, pot and compost; light, temperature, drainage and measurement times.

cards.title: Record
cards.text: On days 0, 3, 7 and 10: each plant’s height in cm from soil to main shoot tip; leaf colour and condition.

cards.title: Care and honesty
cards.text: Check daily. Keep actual records, including any missed measurement or necessary care change.

blocks.prompt: W1. Name the change, measurement and two controls.
W2. Explain the difference between a prediction and a result.

pupilPages.title: Route 1 • Assemble a fair plan
pupilPages.intro: Word bank: water amount / height / same / three / cm.

blocks.prompt: S1. Deliberately change...
S2. Name two conditions to keep comparable.
S3. How many plants are planned in each group?
S4. Describe where the ruler starts and ends.
S5. Future results should be...

pupilPages.title: Route 2 • Write the handover method
pupilPages.intro: Give enough detail for another team to follow the proposed comparison.

blocks.prompt: M1. Write a testable investigation question.
M2. State the change and two controls.
M3. Write a short method including IDs, repeats, height rule and observation days.
M4. State one separate prediction and one care check.

pupilPages.title: Route 3 • Audit the weak plan
pupilPages.intro: Weak plan: “Use one small bean plant in a dark cupboard with 5 mL daily, and one large pea plant in a sunny window with 15 mL. Measure once when convenient.”

blocks.prompt: T1. Identify three confounding differences.
T2. Repair the comparison using matched groups and repeats.
T3. Improve the observation schedule and measurement rule.
T4. A plant becomes severely stressed. What should the adult do, and how should this affect the record?

pupilPages.title: Exit and reflection
pupilPages.intro: Point, draw, write or tell an adult.

blocks.prompt: E1. What factor is this plan changing?
E2. Why use three plants per group?
E3. Should a prediction be copied into the results as a measurement?
R1. Which idea did you improve or defend? What evidence helped?
R2. What useful question would you investigate next?

answers.label: Retrieval 1–3
answers.answer: 1 valid requirement. 2 no: leaf condition/colour also matter. 3 cm.

answers.label: We do W1–W2
answers.answer: W1 water amount; height change plus leaf condition; relevant matched conditions including species, starting size, pot/compost, light or temperature. W2 prediction is expected; a result comes from an observation or measurement actually made.

answers.label: Hinge
answers.answer: First option correct. Second has confounds; third invents evidence.

answers.label: S1–S5
answers.answer: S1 water amount only. S2 two valid controls. S3 three. S4 soil surface to main shoot tip. S5 observed later.

answers.label: M1–M4
answers.answer: M1 how does daily water amount affect these young bean seedlings over 10 days? M2 5 versus 15 mL daily in the fictional plan; two valid controls. M3 label A1–A3/B1–B3; match and allocate seedlings; record baseline; apply planned water; measure soil-to-tip in cm and leaf condition on days 0/3/7/10 at consistent times; keep all records. M4 any reasoned prediction clearly labelled, plus daily care check and adult action if stress.

answers.label: T1–T4
answers.answer: T1 species, starting size and light all differ; water is intended change. T2 three comparable seedlings of one species per group, matched pots/compost and growing conditions, different water amounts only. T3 dated baseline and agreed repeat observations with consistent soil-to-shoot-tip cm measurement and leaf notes. T4 prioritise suitable care, stop/adjust treatment as necessary, record exactly what changed; interpret the result with this limitation.

answers.label: Exit E1–E3
answers.answer: E1 daily water amount. E2 individuals vary; repeats make comparison less dependent on one unusual plant. E3 no.

answers.label: R1–R2
answers.answer: Responses vary. Credit a scientific revision, evidence-based defence or relevant next question. A private or oral response has equal value.

teacherNotes: 40 minutes: opening 2, retrieval 3, I do 7, We do 8, hinge 3, independent 12, review 3, exit 2. Zero-minute slides share the named stage time.
BUILD uses the supplied Year 3 science anchor with age-respectful contexts for older pupils. Supported, standard and stretch are selectable routes within the pathway.

Interactive We do: predict first, test against the controlled SVG model or supplied evidence, then explain or revise. Shared W tasks offer the equivalent paper discussion. Animation is a teaching representation, not filmed experimental evidence.
Keep constructed evidence separate from actual class observations. Do not invent measurements or require internet research.

A real 10-day study cannot be completed within this 40-minute lesson. The next lesson supplies dated constructed data for complete analysis without pretending that time has passed. Optional real observations continue separately.
Secure core: an explicit question, one intended change, relevant controls, repeat plants and honest records.
